items.prompt: A policy assistant handles 100,000 decisions per day across retrieval, Claude calls, and external tools. Incidents are hard to reproduce because operators see only the final answer. Which observability design is appropriate?
constraints: Operators need causal evidence across retrieval, model, and tool stages.
Privacy rules limit unrestricted retention of conversation content.

options.text: Store the final answer and availability, then rerun the same question during an incident and compare the later response with the operator's memory of the failure.
Retain complete prompts, tool results, and model responses for a fixed incident-retention period in one broadly searchable archive so investigators can search content without a trace schema.
Record model version, request count, and monthly uptime, and ask service owners to add detail only when a repeated incident becomes severe.
Emit correlated structured traces for configuration, retrieval, model and tool spans, resource use, failure class, and outcome, with privacy-aware content handling.

feedback.Reason: A final answer cannot explain which retrieval or tool path caused a failure, while unrestricted raw retention violates the privacy constraint. Correlated structured spans provide causal signal with controlled content.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: A trace ID links the run and child spans; metadata, versions, timings, resource use, and outcome classifications diagnose execution without requiring every protected payload by default.
Details.scenarioApplication: Trace retrieval query and evidence IDs, model configuration, tool calls and results, and final task outcome, redacting or restricting content according to policy.
Details.errorCorrection: Instrument the execution graph and outcome, not only the response or uptime, and make data minimization part of the telemetry design.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Structured tracing and sampling require schema and storage discipline, but they make high-volume failures reproducible without building an unrestricted transcript lake.
Details.transfer: At scale, correlate each execution stage to an outcome and retain only the content needed for an authorized diagnosis.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Rerunning later may use different data or configuration and still cannot show which stage failed in the original execution.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: A broad raw archive, even with fixed retention, increases privacy and search exposure and does not provide structured causal spans for retrieval, model, or tool diagnosis.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Model version and volume cannot distinguish retrieval, tool, latency, or outcome failures.

items.prompt: A policy assistant's accuracy drops after a tool-description revision, while uptime and average latency remain unchanged. Request IDs, tool-call spans, and prompt versions exist, but there is no comparison dashboard. What diagnosis should come first?
constraints: A successful transport call can still select the wrong tool or evidence.
Existing traces can be compared by version and task outcome.

options.text: Roll back the tool description and every related infrastructure change, then attribute recovery to the description because it was the most recent release.
Compare versioned traces and evaluation outcomes for tool selection, parameters, retrieval evidence, and answer correctness before changing infrastructure.
Raise output-token limits and retry completed calls, assuming unchanged uptime means the model needs more generation capacity rather than a different tool path.
Compare only API error rates by release, treating any request that returned HTTP success as correct for the policy task.

feedback.Reason: The changed description can alter tool selection or arguments without affecting transport health. Versioned traces and task outcomes can isolate that path before a broad rollback or tuning change.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Join prompt/tool versions to selected operation, parameters, evidence, and outcome labels; compare matched cases to locate the changed decision boundary.
Details.scenarioApplication: Build a release comparison for tool selection accuracy, valid parameters, retrieval support, and answer correctness, then test a targeted description repair.
Details.errorCorrection: Separate transport success from task success and use the execution evidence already captured to diagnose the changed configuration.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Trace analysis and a holdout evaluation take time, but they avoid changing unrelated infrastructure and preserve causal attribution.
Details.transfer: When quality changes without availability changes, compare versioned execution paths and outcome labels before treating the issue as capacity.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: A broad rollback confounds the tool-description change with unrelated infrastructure and cannot explain which path recovered.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: More output capacity does not test tool selection or retrieval evidence and may increase cost without addressing the changed contract.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Transport success can mask a wrong tool or unsupported answer, so API error rate is not a task-quality diagnosis.

items.prompt: A healthcare triage assistant handles protected patient information. Engineers need to understand slow runs and wrong tool calls, but default telemetry must minimize sensitive content. Which telemetry boundary is defensible?
constraints: Operational metadata must support latency and tool diagnosis.
Protected content needs minimization, controlled access, and bounded retention.

options.text: Log every patient prompt, retrieved passage, and tool result indefinitely so investigators can reconstruct any run without requesting special access.
Disable tracing by default and retain only monthly uptime and volume, avoiding protected content at the cost of stage-level diagnosis.
Keep correlated metadata and redacted outcomes by default, and capture sampled content only under explicit access, purpose, and retention controls.
Store model name and request count, then ask clinicians to describe the slow or wrong tool run from memory during the incident review.

feedback.Reason: The default must retain enough signal to locate slow or wrong stages without creating an unrestricted patient transcript. Metadata-first tracing with controlled samples balances diagnosis and minimization.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Run and span IDs, timings, configuration, tool names, status, and redacted outcome fields reveal causal behavior; content samples are separately authorized and time-limited.
Details.scenarioApplication: Trace a triage run and its tool calls by ID, redact patient fields, restrict any incident sample to approved investigators, and delete it on the defined schedule.
Details.errorCorrection: Treat privacy as a telemetry boundary with explicit sampling and retention, not as a reason to erase the execution graph.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Some incidents require an approved content sample and may remain partly unresolved, but default logging does not expose protected data unnecessarily.
Details.transfer: For sensitive AI systems, preserve stage-level operational evidence by default and gate content capture with purpose, access, and retention controls.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Indefinite raw capture violates minimization and retention boundaries and creates a larger breach surface than the diagnosis requires.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Suppressing traces removes the timing and tool evidence needed to diagnose production failures.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Model name and count cannot explain a slow span or wrong tool, and memory-based reconstruction is incomplete.

items.prompt: A research workflow runs several agents and tools in parallel. Average latency is acceptable, but p95 spikes intermittently and users report incomplete reports. Which TWO telemetry priorities are most useful? Select TWO.
constraints: The failure may occur in one branch while aggregate averages remain normal.
The report outcome must be joined to the worker and tool execution path.

options.text: Track only final report length and daily average latency so the monitoring dashboard stays simple.
Emit correlated per-step timing and status for each worker, tool, retrieval, and synthesis span, segmented by deployment version.
Keep permanent unrestricted copies of all conversations so analysts can search for any missing section later.
Alert on the mean latency and sample a single worker log whenever the daily average changes.
Record worker, evidence, synthesis, and report-completeness outcomes so a missing section can be traced to a branch and release.

feedback.Reason: Tail latency and incomplete reports require both per-branch execution timing and an outcome join. Averages or report length alone hide the failed branch; raw transcripts add privacy risk without causal structure.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Parent and child span IDs connect parallel workers and retries; segmented timings and outcome labels reveal which branch or release produced the missing section.
Details.scenarioApplication: Track start/end/status and evidence counts per worker and tool, join them to the synthesis and completeness result, and alert on p95 or branch failure classes.
Details.errorCorrection: Instrument the execution graph and user-relevant completion outcome instead of relying on aggregate activity metrics.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: More structured dimensions increase dashboard and cardinality management, but they make intermittent branch failures diagnosable.
Details.transfer: For parallel AI workflows, correlate child timing and evidence with the final outcome and retain high-level signals that preserve privacy.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Report length and daily averages cannot identify a slow or failed branch or distinguish a concise complete report from an incomplete one.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Permanent raw copies increase privacy and retention risk and still lack reliable parent-child causality unless structured IDs are propagated.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Mean alerts and one sampled log can miss the p95 branch and the worker that caused a missing section.

omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.b: Without per-step correlated timing and status, intermittent tail behavior cannot be localized to a worker, tool, or release.
omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.e: Without outcome links, telemetry cannot show which branch or evidence path caused the incomplete report.

items.prompt: A low-rate tool authorization failure affects 0.1% of requests, while 1% head sampling captures only successful traffic. Operators cannot explain denied calls or their latency tails. Which sampling design should be tested?
constraints: Sampling must retain rare failures and tail-latency evidence.
Sensitive payloads must not become an unrestricted default log.

options.text: Keep uniform head sampling at one percent and infer denied-call behavior from successful traffic because the rate and collector configuration are stable.
Capture complete conversations for a fixed extended retention period so the rare failure class is unlikely to be missed, without creating a separate error-triggered sampling stratum.
Use error- and latency-triggered sampling with bounded retention, stratified metadata by tool and version, and redacted or access-controlled sensitive fields.
Increase uniform head sampling until the expected failure count is statistically visible, but keep the same payload retention and no error-triggered stratum.

feedback.Reason: Uniform head sampling is demonstrably missing the rare class. Triggered sampling can preserve failure and tail evidence while metadata redaction and retention bounds keep privacy exposure controlled.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: The collector samples error and latency thresholds separately from ordinary traffic, labels tool and version, and applies access and retention policy to any content fields.
Details.scenarioApplication: Retain denied-call metadata and span timing at high recall, sample authorized payloads only when approved, and measure whether the design captures the incident class.
Details.errorCorrection: Design sampling around failure and tail observability, not only volume, and keep content handling separate from event selection.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Triggered streams add collector and storage rules, but they provide evidence for rare incidents without logging all successful conversations.
Details.transfer: For low-rate failures, stratify by error and latency, bound retention, and verify that the sample captures the class needed for diagnosis.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Successful head samples cannot explain a failure class they never capture, regardless of how predictable the sample rate is.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Capturing complete conversations can preserve the rare event, but broadly retaining their sensitive payloads exceeds the metadata and controlled samples needed for this diagnosis.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Increasing uniform sampling may still miss 0.1% events and does not guarantee retention of the tail or protect sensitive content.

items.prompt: A lead agent launches asynchronous workers through a queue. Worker logs contain local request IDs, but the final report cannot identify which worker, retrieval result, or retry caused a missing section. What trace change is needed?
constraints: Each child execution and retry must remain joinable to the lead run.
The report completeness outcome must link to the causal execution path without raw research content.

options.text: Propagate the parent run identifier through queue messages, emit structured child spans and evidence links, and join them to the report-completeness result in the trace store.
Inspect workers' independent logs manually and compare queue depth with the final report whenever a user reports a missing section.
Store only the final report and aggregate queue depth, reasoning that child identifiers would expose research content and are unnecessary for diagnosis.
Assign a fresh trace ID to each retry and aggregate the IDs after synthesis, preserving local isolation while losing the original parent-child chain.

feedback.Reason: Local IDs cannot establish parent-child causality. Propagating a run ID and recording structured child, evidence, and retry links lets operators trace the missing section without storing the research text itself.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Queue metadata carries a parent and child span identity; the trace store joins worker outcomes and evidence handles to the lead synthesis and completeness result.
Details.scenarioApplication: Create a child span for every worker and retry, attach retrieval IDs and status, and mark which report section consumed each artifact.
Details.errorCorrection: Preserve causal identity across asynchronous boundaries rather than relying on independent logs or aggregate queue health.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Identifier propagation and trace joins add schema and queue plumbing, but they turn an intermittent missing section into an inspectable execution path.
Details.transfer: For queued or parallel agents, carry parent-child trace context and connect evidence and final outcomes while keeping sensitive content governed separately.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Manual log inspection and queue depth cannot prove which worker or retrieval artifact caused a specific report gap.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Final output and queue depth lack the child path needed for diagnosis; identifiers themselves need not contain research content.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Independent IDs without a propagated parent link make it impossible to relate a retry to the lead run; retries should use child spans under the same trace.

items.prompt:
A healthcare incident review is authorized by the privacy officer for 30 minutes. The reviewer needs exact redacted excerpts to explain one wrong tool call; ordinary telemetry remains metadata-only and raw content is encrypted with access logging.

Which telemetry policy supports this authorized, time-limited incident review?
constraints: The privacy officer authorizes one reviewer and a 30-minute review with specified request IDs and redaction.
The exact redacted excerpt is needed to explain one wrong tool call.
Ordinary telemetry remains metadata-only; raw content is encrypted, access logged, and deletable.

options.text: Keep telemetry metadata-only even during the authorized review because content must never enter observability.
Capture all raw conversations for the incident window so future investigators can inspect any possible cause.
Store the redacted sample indefinitely in the observability archive so later incidents can reuse it.
Capture only the approved redacted sample under its 30-minute controls; keep metadata by default and delete the sample afterward.

feedback.Reason: The decision changes only under an explicit purpose, access, redaction, and retention grant, preserving privacy as the default.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic emphasizes high-level patterns that provide operational signal without exposing conversation contents when privacy matters. The scenario's mechanism is governed by this decisive constraint: The privacy boundary now explicitly authorizes narrowly scoped content sampling, so metadata-only telemetry is insufficient for this incident while broad raw capture remains prohibited.
Details.scenarioApplication: Capture the approved redacted content sample for the affected trace under the 30-minute retention and access controls, retain correlated metadata by default, and delete the sample when the review ends.
Details.errorCorrection: The reviewer cannot distinguish the wrong tool argument from a valid one without the approved excerpt, so the incident remains unresolved despite a permitted narrow exception.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the privacy approval or redaction pipeline fails, revert to metadata-only traces and publish the incident as unresolved rather than retaining raw content.
Details.transfer: Route each information need through the smallest governed interface that matches its evidence shape, and preserve explicit authorization, freshness, and unavailable states when the evidence cannot support a claim.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: The reviewer cannot distinguish the wrong tool argument from a valid one without the approved excerpt, so the incident remains unresolved despite the permitted narrow exception.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Broad raw capture exceeds the approved purpose and retention boundary; the authorization covers a narrow redacted sample only.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: The sample is authorized for a 30-minute review, so indefinite retention exceeds purpose and retention controls even after redaction.

items.prompt:
Resolution acceptance falls from 82% to 74% after a prompt and retrieval release, while transport success remains 99.9% and p95 stays within target. Product must decide whether to roll back the prompt, repair retrieval, or accept the change.

Which observability change should precede a rollback or targeted repair?
constraints: Acceptance falls from 82% to 74%, while transport success and p95 remain healthy.
Current traces include technical IDs but do not join to the human resolution outcome.
A 2,000-case labeled replay can compare prompt and retrieval versions, and acceptance is the value metric.

options.text: Join traces to outcome IDs, compare prompt/retrieval versions, and target rollback or repair to the component explaining the loss.
Keep the release because uptime and p95 are healthy, or roll back the entire stack without tracing the resolution outcome.
Roll back both prompt and retrieval immediately, then add outcome tracing after the incident is closed.
Compare only transport traces and request latency by deployment, using the existing IDs as a proxy for acceptance.

feedback.Reason: The missing business join is the decisive observability defect; it prevents choosing between prompt and retrieval repairs from transport metrics alone.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Tracing helps reveal poor queries, sources, and tool failures that are otherwise hard to diagnose in production. The scenario's mechanism is governed by this decisive constraint: Observability must join technical spans to the business outcome and slice before a rollback or repair decision; healthy uptime and p95 do not explain the 8-point outcome drop.
Details.scenarioApplication: Add outcome IDs and resolution events to the trace, compare prompt/retrieval versions on the labeled replay and affected traffic, then roll back or repair the component whose evidence explains the acceptance loss.
Details.errorCorrection: The first choice ignores the actual business regression, while the second destroys evidence needed to identify the responsible component and preserve a targeted repair.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the outcome join shows acceptance recovered within the same release and the dip was an annotation artifact, keep the deployment and repair measurement instead.
Details.transfer: Route each information need through the smallest governed interface that matches its evidence shape, and preserve explicit authorization, freshness, and unavailable states when the evidence cannot support a claim.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Healthy transport does not explain the business regression, while a broad rollback destroys evidence needed to identify the responsible component.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Immediate broad rollback may reduce symptoms but cannot distinguish the responsible component or preserve a targeted repair decision.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Transport and latency are not the value outcome; without resolution joins the eight-point acceptance loss remains unexplained.
